newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks higher at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks higher at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks moved higher at midday Monday as takeover talk fuelled buying interest and high-tech issues continued their bounce from late last week.
The dollar's four-year high against the yen and a strong U.S. Treasury market supported stocks.
The Dow Jones industrial average was up 46.46 points, or .71 percent, at 6,572.53 at 1 p.m. EDT. Big Board advances led declining issues 16-7 on volume of about 254 million shares.
Regional investment bank stocks rose sharply on views they are likely takeover candidates after giant Bankers Trust New York Corp. proposed a $1.7 billion acquisition of brokerage Alex. Brown Inc.

"The changes in the Federal Reserve regulations allowing banks to get a larger percentage of the revenues of their brokerage operations have opened the door," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"Every so often, a transaction comes along that re-ignites the speculation in brokerage stocks. There will be more, and each time they will restimulate interest in brokers," he said.

Alex. Brown stock leaped 10-3/8 to 63-1/2 while Bankers Trust was down 1-7/8 at 80-3/8. Legg Mason Inc. jumped 4-5/8 to 49-5/8, Morgan Keegan Inc. rose 2-1/8 to 19 and Piper Jaffray Cos. gained 2-1/4 to 17.
Oppenheimer & Co.'s chief investment strategist, Michael Metz, said the rise in those stocks was helping restimulate the market's "speculative juices."
"Investors have gotten their courage up because they see no potential negatives on the horizon in terms of (economic) data."
U.S. Treasury bonds were higher, with the long bond up half a point to yield 7.08 percent, down from 7.12 percent Friday.

The dollar was trading at 1.7085 marks and 125.61 yen, off the 125.72 yen it reached earlier, but still up from 124.27 late Friday and its highest level against the Japanese currency since January of 1993.
The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite Index was up 18.46 points, or 1.49 percent, at 1,255.

High-tech stocks extended their gains from last week. Cisco Systems Inc. was the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, up 3-3/8 at 54-1/4. Intel Corp. was up 3-1/2 at 158-1/2, Microsoft Corp. gained 3-3/16 to 97-3/8, and International Business Machines Corp. was up 3-3/4 at 132-7/8.
Cowen & Co. reiterated a strong buy rating on Cisco Systems, while Oppenheimer & Co. re-issued its outperform rating on Cisco.

"Techs give you the most bang for your buck," Metz said. "They have rebounded, but they will lead us down in a few sessions. They are the most vulnerable to earnings disappointments and to a downward revision in valuations because of higher interest rates. People will start to sell them after they climb another 2 or 3 percent."

Stock in Rational Software Corp. dropped 10-1/16 to 13-5/16 after Alex. Brown said it cut its rating on the stock to market perform from strong buy. The company said it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Pure Atria Corp., exchanging 0.90 share of Rational for each Pure Atria share. Pure Atria stock was down 7-1/4 at 10-1/2.
Allegheny Power System Inc. and DQE Inc.'s Duquesne Light Co. agreed to a $10.6 billion merger. Allegheny was down 7/8 at 28-7/8. DQE stock was up 2-1/4 at 29-3/8.
Nike Inc. stock fell 4-3/4 to 54-1/2 and topped the NYSE most active list. Smith Barney downgraded the stock to neutral from outperform.
